summary: Willamette NF lookout near Oakridge: a 1919 pole tower, a 1934 22-foot L-4 tower and a 1958 R-6 tower; removed or destroyed in 1968.

facts.design: 22-foot round timber tower with an L-4 cab (1934), then a treated timber tower with an R-6 cab (1958)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1968 per the registry and the Rex's page; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968

events.note: 10-foot pole tower with a shake cabin
August 24, 1932: Eugene Guard, as quoted on Rex's page, reported that new lookout houses would be built at He-He Mountain and several other sites
Pole tower replaced with a 22-foot round timber tower with an L-4 cab (model 1931 cab per the Rex's page)
Replaced with a treated timber tower with an R-6 flat-roof cab
Registry and Rex's page say the lookout was removed
firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968 (conflicts with removed)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register May 7, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: All three detail pages describe timber towers: a 10-foot pole tower (1919), a 22-foot round timber tower (1934) and a treated timber tower (1958). The Forest Fire Lookout Association list (source 4) labels the site Ground, which the editor should confirm before the record changes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The registry and the Rex's page say the lookout was removed in 1968; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968. The story reports both and does not pick a cause.

notes_for_editor: The 1919, 1934 and 1958 structures agree across the registry and firelookout.com; the Rex's page agrees on 1934, 1958 and 1968. Removed versus destroyed in 1968 is the one conflict. The 1932 Eugene Guard line is quoted second-hand from the Rex's page and was not checked against the newspaper. A WebSearch on the Willamette history and a Cox 1991 lookout report turned up nothing usable, so they are not cited. The 6.7 m height is the 22-foot 1934 tower, not the 1958 structure. Nothing describes the site today; the kind correction would change the map marker, so confirm the Ground label first.
